coverage_gaps: PubMed-only retrieval may miss authoritative variant-curation records, preprints, conference findings, patents, and non-indexed historical material.
Terminology and abstract indexing may omit substrate names or negative findings, reducing recall for older and null-result studies.
Ancestry-specific penetrance and rare-variant evidence may remain uneven because cohort size, ascertainment, and reporting differ across populations.
Direct physiological relevance in human dopaminergic neurons and brain tissue may be less developed than biochemical, immune-cell, or animal-model evidence.
Publication bias may limit retrieval of failed replications, absent phenotypes, and negative substrate experiments.
exclusion_criteria: Records with only incidental mention of LRRK2 and no extractable genetic, biochemical, cellular, or disease-mechanistic evidence.
Variant catalogs or case reports lacking sufficient evidence to classify pathogenicity, risk, protection, or uncertainty.
Purely computational substrate predictions without biochemical, cellular, tissue, or genetic validation.
Claims based solely on overexpression when no appropriate control, endogenous confirmation, or explicit limitation is available.
Therapeutic efficacy reports that do not inform LRRK2 target engagement, mechanism, substrate biology, or safety-related interpretation.
Narrative reviews used as sole support for a central historical, genetic, or mechanistic claim when the cited primary study can be retrieved.
inclusion_criteria: Publication date is on or before 2024-12-31.
The record reports primary data or a rigorous synthesis directly concerning LRRK2/PARK8 and Parkinson disease, LRRK2 enzymology, or disease-relevant physiological substrates.
Genetic claims include interpretable evidence such as linkage, segregation, allele frequency, association statistics, ancestry, penetrance, or functional validation.
Mechanistic claims identify the experimental system, perturbation or variant, assay, comparator, and measured biochemical or cellular outcome.
Substrate claims distinguish direct phosphorylation evidence from downstream association and preferentially include endogenous or in vivo validation.
Limitation evidence is eligible when it tests penetrance, reproducibility, specificity, model validity, species generality, or human relevance.
Landmark primary studies are prioritized for discovery and mechanism claims; systematic reviews or meta-analyses are used to contextualize consistency and population effects.

question_frame: Search PubMed from database inception through 2024-12-31 for human genetic, biochemical, cellular, animal-model, and human-biospecimen evidence linking leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2/PARK8/dardarin) to Parkinson disease. Reconstruct the genetic discovery and variant spectrum; distinguish pathogenic, risk, protective, and uncertain variants; evaluate kinase and ROC-COR GTPase mechanisms, Rab-family and other proposed physiological substrates, downstream trafficking and lysosomal biology, and evidence limiting causal strength, penetrance, substrate generality, or model-to-human translation.
stop_rules: Stop landmark discovery searching after the original linkage and gene-identification reports plus independent confirmation papers are captured and backward citation leads add no new discovery event.
Stop variant expansion after pathogenic, common risk, protective, and uncertain classes are represented across major ancestry contexts and two consecutive query refinements yield no new class.
Stop enzymology searching after kinase, ROC-COR GTPase, variant-specific effects, and their coupling are supported by convergent biochemical evidence with explicit controls.

Stop substrate searching after direct-site, endogenous, inhibitor-sensitive, and in vivo evidence is assessed for the principal Rab substrates and two consecutive refinements add no new validated substrate class.
Stop pathway searching when vesicle, lysosomal, autophagy or mitophagy, and relevant neural or immune-cell evidence can be linked to enzymatic outputs with model limitations recorded.
Stop challenge searching only after incomplete penetrance, nonmanifesting carriers, conflicting substrate or model findings, and human-translation limits each have at least one eligible source.

Stop the full retrieval when every requested section has supporting and limiting evidence, all included records satisfy the cutoff, and the final update query produces no material change to the mechanistic synthesis.
